The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. ### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the net diff implies, judged against objectui's runner at the pin.

1. **The effective-executor resolution is the runner's, exactly — RIGHT.** `effectiveRowExecutor` reads `row[executorKey] || row.name`. The runner reads `action.type || action.actionType || action.name || ''` (`core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts:1265` at the pin; the same line, byte-unchanged, at objectui `origin/main` `72594f29`, and `packages/components/src/renderers/action/` unchanged between the two). All four renderers hand the runner an explicit object, never a spread of the schema: `type: schema.actionType, name: schema.name` (`action-button.tsx`, `action-icon.tsx`) and `type: action.type, name: action.name` (`action-group.tsx`, `action-menu.tsx`), with no `actionType` key. So on a node the runner's three legs collapse to `actionType || name`, on a member to `type || name`, which is what the helper computes. The operator is `||`, as the runner writes it: an empty executor key falls through to `name` at the click and so at the parse; the dev's correction of triage's `??` transcription is measured and right. `handlers.has(actionType)` and `builtinExecutors[actionType]` are exact-key lookups with no case folding, so the untouched `name: 'URL'` control is right.
2. **The url navigator's reach is exactly `url` and `navigation` — RIGHT.** `builtinExecutors` sends `url` to `executeUrl` (`target || redirect`) and `navigation` to `executeNavigation` (`to || target || redirect`); those are the only two rows that call `navigateTo` (`form`, `modal`, `flow`, `api`, `script` do not). A host handler wins before a built-in, and no host registers one under either name at the pin (`registerHandler` names across `packages/app-shell` and `apps`: `api`, `create`, `crud_success`, `delete`, `dialog_cancel`, `flow`, `navigate`, `navigate_create`, `navigate_edit`, `refresh`, `script`). The legacy `action.navigate` fallback needs a key the strict rows do not declare, and `to` / `redirect` are not row keys, so `target` is the one value both executors open: judging `target` is complete.
3. **Applied on every row it should be, and nowhere else — RIGHT.** The refinement sits on `ActionButtonPropsSchema` and `ActionIconPropsSchema` (key `actionType`) and on `buildActionGroupMember` and `buildActionMenuMember` (key `type`): the four `ComponentPropsMap` rows that forward a free executor key beside a `name`. No other door opens a name leg: `ActionSchema.type` is the required closed `ActionType` enum (`action.zod.ts:1017`), so an `action:bar` spread of a registered action carries a typed executor; the `element:button` inline action keeps its own `navigation`-onto-`url` fold; the dashboard header action already judges an omitted `actionType` (PR #23101). `navigation-target.ts`, `refuseRowUrlExecutorAlias` and every other refinement are untouched.
4. **`name` is left unrefused, as triage ordered — RIGHT.** The diff adds no issue at `name`; the only new issue path is `target`. A row whose `name` is any other handler (`navigate_edit`, `navigate_create`, `convert_lead`, `flow`, `api`, `URL`) and a row with neither key nor name parse as before, pinned in `component-action-row-effective-executor.test.ts` and in the lint test's other-handler control.
5. **A declared executor key still outranks `name` — RIGHT.** `||` is left-to-right: `actionType: 'url'` with `name: 'convert_lead'` is refused exactly as before, and `flow` / `script` / `api` / `modal` / `form` / `navigate_edit` at the key with `name: 'url'` leave `target` alone, both pinned on all four rows.
6. **One URL grammar, the control byte-identical — RIGHT.** The only judge is `navigationTargetRefusal` (file untouched). The subject is reassembled from the owner, `` `target` `` and a spelling parenthetical; for a key-spelled executor the parenthetical is `` `actionType: 'url'` ``, so the control reads `` An `action:button`'s `target` (`actionType: 'url'`) `` and its three siblings exactly as before, which the untouched `url-target-doors.test.ts` pins (lines 166 to 172) beside the new file's own control. The name-leg subject (`` `name: 'url'` and no `actionType`, so the runner runs the url navigator ``) and its empty-key variant (`` an empty `actionType` ``) change the parenthetical only; everything after it is the grammar's own text.
7. **`navigation` at the executor key is now refused at two paths — RIGHT, and the key refusal is unchanged.** The alias rule from PR #23164 still refuses at `actionType` / `type` with the rename; the effective executor is `navigation`, so `target` is judged too. One row, two issues, pinned.
8. **The props gate reports it with no lint code change — RIGHT.** `validateComponentProps` parses `properties` against the same `ComponentPropsMap` rows; the new lint cases pin `properties.target` and `properties.actions.0.target` with the first sentence above. `validate-component-props.ts` is untouched, which keeps clear of PR #23244.
9. **Describes and the regenerated reference — RIGHT, with one non-blocking nit.** Eight `component.mdx` lines move, `name` and `target` on the four shapes, matching the describes. Nit: the describes say "no `actionType`" / "no `type`", while the refinement, the D3 entry and the refusal text also cover an EMPTY key; the author is told "an empty `actionType`" at the point of refusal, so nothing misleads. Carry the word into the describes when these rows are next touched.
10. **The docs-drift advisory names nothing this diff falsifies — RIGHT.** `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` restates no row rule, and `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`'s only `actionType: 'url'` is a dashboard header action example. The four release pages are read-only and unaffected.
11. **No partial or silent `onSuccess` half — RIGHT.** No refinement, describe, test or D3 text on `onSuccess` is touched; `component-action-row-on-success-executor.test.ts` is untouched; the rows' `onSuccess` stays `ActionSchema`'s block by reference as PR #23164 landed it.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23168-page-action-row-name-leg-url-target.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **`minor`**, **BREAKING** under the launch-window convention for accept-set narrowings, the form the family's landed changeset (`23103-page-action-row-on-success-and-executor.md`) and the v17 release pages state. It carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the ADR-0087 `registered` marker naming `ui-page-action-row-name-leg-url-target-judged`, a FROM → TO table (schemes, `//host`, bare relative, the empty string, the `navigation` name) and the one-line fix. RIGHT.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right arm**: no key, value or export is added or widened; rows accepted before are refused now and nothing else moves. Not `skip-changeset`: it publishes from a released package.
- **D3 entry** `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-page-action-row-name-leg-url-target-judged.ts`: filename derived from the id, the same major as its siblings, a typed `SemanticMigration` with surface, replacement, reason and acceptanceCriteria, no `conversionIds` (marked NOT mechanically convertible, as `ui-page-action-row-url-target-scheme-set-closed` is), no `relevantWhen` (none of the family's entries is in the relevance table), and no tracker number in its prose. `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide` ride `Lint & Repo Gates` / `TypeScript Type Check`, both green on this head. RIGHT.
- `ROADMAP.md` untouched, as in PRs #23101 and #23164. Fine.

### ③ Boundary flags

Report `6148078184`, every deviation and the out-of-scope entry:

1. `Part of #23168` instead of the dispatch's `Fixes` — **answered, right**: the remainder is in triage's box, the body carries no closing keyword, and `Part-of PR must not also close its card` is green.
2. The `onSuccess` rule not implemented — **answered, right**: the dispatch's fork clause tripped on two measured objectui producers, and ① 11 confirms nothing was narrowed silently.
3. Model-free commit trailers (AGENTS.md's pair) over the harness reminder — **answered, right**: AGENTS.md outranks the reminder and the pre-push hook refuses a model id; verified on `28251e51d` and `b76c26a99`. The merge commit `f1a31cee7` carries no trailer pair (the merge script's own form); squash landing makes that moot. Non-blocking.
4. Self-inflicted PREREQUISITE NOT MET noise on 8 spec/lint gates — **answered**: the reruns at the same head exit 0, and the head's `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are the verdicts, both green.
5. Two MODULE_NOT_FOUND first suite runs — **answered**: reruns after building the closures; CI runs the farm.
6. An inline `bash -c` rerun loop blocked and replaced by a script — process only, no contract effect.
7. A probe script briefly in `packages/spec`, moved before any commit — **answered**: the 6-file list holds no probe.
8. The spec full suite read at `b76c26a99`, before the merge — **answered**: the merge brought nothing under `packages/spec` or `packages/lint` (diff read); `Test Core` on this head is the verdict and is in progress at this record.
- **out_of_scope_findings[0]**: `ActionSchema`'s `onSuccess` refusal gives a false reason (`action.zod.ts:2209` to `2212`, for `modal` / `flow` / `form`: "no renderer reads a post-success hop today"), while the runner's `handlePostExecution` runs after every built-in and every host handler at the pin. The refusal is right; the reason is not. **Escalated, not blocking**: it rides the `onSuccess` half's PR, which rewrites that rule's reach, and the open card holds it in the report and in the seat's ACCEPT. If that half is split off this card, file it as its own card rather than leaving it in a closed thread.
- **open_questions** (the A / B / C fork and the `Fixes` line) are with triage, and **this head prejudges neither**: no `onSuccess` refinement, describe or test moves, and `Part of` keeps the card open. Triage's fourth pin ("a navigating row with `onSuccess` is refused") is therefore NOT delivered by this head, by design: read this PASS as the name-leg half only.
